title: Prom and Recipe
premise: Wendell Amberdale, seventeen and de facto parent to two younger siblings while their mother works hospital night shifts, has survived twelve years in the fading town of Marrow Creek by being careful, quiet, and invisible. When their best friend Priya vanishes the night of the spring bake-off, leaving only a ring of keys and a half-finished recipe card, Wendell discovers she was investigating the town's beloved Founder's Day prom tradition—and the scholarship fund that quietly eats the futures of kids like them. As Wendell, the siblings, and a reluctant prom-committee insider dig through decades of ledgers, they find the 'tradition' is a machine for disappearing inconvenient teenagers, and Priya's disappearance is only the latest. To force the truth into the open, Wendell must do the one thing they've never dared: be seen, loudly, at prom itself—exposing the fund's trustees, finding Priya alive and hiding in the old cannery, and choosing found family over the safety of silence.
about_author: Juniper Nystrom is the pen name of a former small-town bakery counter worker who grew up in a mill town where the prom was the biggest event of the year. They write stories about kids who raise each other, and they still can't frost a cake without eating the evidence.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A morning in the Amberdale house: packing lunches, hiding the overdue electric bill, getting siblings Theo and Birdie to school before their mother's night-shift bus returns. Establishes Wendell's invisible, hyper-competent survival mode. Emotional beat: love expressed as logistics, and the ache of being a kid no one parents.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Porch
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Priya misses their standing Thursday study session—unprecedented in nine years of friendship. On Wendell's porch sit Priya's bike keys, house keys, and a recipe card for marzipan prom cake, half-burned at one corner. Wendell reports to the police; Officer Daneau is polite and dismissive. Emotional beat: the first crack in Wendell's careful world.

chapters.title: Everyone Says She Ran
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. School the next day: whispers that Priya ran away, that her family was 'difficult.' Priya's younger brother Devi begs Wendell to find her, and Wendell can't say no. Emotional beat: guilt—Wendell was so busy surviving they missed whatever Priya was carrying.

chapters.title: What the Recipe Card Says
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Examining the recipe card, Wendell realizes the 'ingredients' are numbers—account figures, dates, initials. Theo, a math whiz, spots that the numbers match the Founders' Prom Scholarship Fund amounts from the library's old newspapers. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose; the careful kid starts taking risks.

chapters.title: Prom, the Town's One Crown
chapters.summary: Birdie's POV. Birdie, ten, narrates the mythology of Marrow Creek's Founder's Day prom—the whole town attends, alumni return, the marzipan cake is a century-old tradition. Birdie adores it and doesn't understand why Wendell flinches. Emotional beat: innocence showing what the town means to the people it's failing.

chapters.title: The Committee's Smile
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell approaches prom committee chair Corliss Vane, the town's golden benefactor, asking about the scholarship. Corliss is warm, generous, and offers Wendell a 'work-study' spot on the committee—an obvious buy-off. Emotional beat: the seductive relief of being offered a way out, and Wendell's suspicion of their own relief.

chapters.title: Devi's List of Last Days
chapters.summary: Wendell and Devi's alternating POV. Devi shares his timeline of Priya's final week: she visited the county records office, interviewed a dropout named Cass Merrow, and stopped sleeping. Wendell tracks down Cass, now working at the cannery. Emotional beat: two grieving kids becoming a team out of necessity.

chapters.title: Cass Merrow Doesn't Do Reunions
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass, who left school at sixteen after 'winning' the scholarship that then vanished, refuses to talk—until Wendell mentions the recipe card. Cass goes pale: Priya interviewed them about the fund three weeks ago, then the questions stopped. Emotional beat: fear; Cass warns Wendell that asking got Priya followed.

chapters.title: Night Shift Economics
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Mom comes home at dawn; a rare honest conversation where Wendell almost tells her everything but swallows it—she's exhausted, and the family needs stability more than truth. Emotional beat: the cost of being the responsible one; loyalty to Mom's fragile peace versus loyalty to Priya.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Stage
chapters.summary: Wendell and Cass's POV. Breaking into the community hall where prom is held, they find a locked storage room under the stage. Inside: decades of scholarship ledgers. Winners' names, then crossed-out names, then blank lines where names should be. Emotional beat: dread—the tradition has a hidden accounting.

chapters.title: Theo Does the Math
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reconciles the ledgers with the fund's public donations and finds a siphon: roughly forty percent of every year's scholarship money flows to a shell entity called Marrow Holdings. Theo is terrified but thrilled to finally matter. Emotional beat: the quiet sibling stepping into the light.

chapters.title: Corliss Makes It Easy
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Corliss increases Wendell's committee 'stipend,' arranges a grocery 'donation,' and offers to cover Birdie's school fees. It would solve everything. Wendell accepts—then hates themselves for it. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; corruption as kindness.

chapters.title: Birdie Asks the Wrong Question
chapters.summary: Birdie's POV. Birdie, helping with prom decorations, overhears Corliss on the phone saying 'the Merrow girl was handled' and innocently repeats it at dinner. The house goes cold. Emotional beat: innocence as detonator; the family can no longer pretend this is safe.

chapters.title: The Van on Amber Street
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A gray van idles outside the house for two nights. Wendell starts sleeping in shifts with a baseball bat, teaching Theo and Birdie a code knock. Mom notices the tension and Wendell finally tells her a partial truth: Priya is missing and Wendell is looking. Emotional beat: fear made domestic; the family closing ranks.

chapters.title: Marzipan and Memory
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass reveals the prom cake's history: the marzipan recipe belonged to the cannery workers' union, and the 'Founders' who endowed the fund were the mill owners who broke the strike in 1954. The prom was invented as a loyalty ritual. Emotional beat: the town's beloved tradition revealed as a leash.

chapters.title: Devi Gets a Message
chapters.summary: Wendell and Devi's POV. Devi receives a text from Priya's old number: 'STOP ASKING. I'M FINE. DON'T TRUST THE KEYS.' But the phrasing is wrong—Priya never capitalizes, never says 'fine.' Someone has her phone. Wendell realizes Priya may be alive and coerced. Emotional beat: hope and terror braided together.

chapters.title: The Alumni Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell interviews former scholarship 'winners' at the diner: each got money, then debt, then a quiet exit from town—one now works for Marrow Holdings. They confirm the pattern: the fund buys silence and ships out anyone who asks questions. Emotional beat: Wendell seeing their own future mapped out and rejected.

chapters.title: Mom's Night Off
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Mom, a nurse, recognizes the signs of a family under siege and confronts Wendell with everything she's pieced together—she knew about the van. She gives Wendell her blessing and her one rule: no one goes alone. Emotional beat: the parent-child roles finally rebalancing; Mom choosing truth over stability.

chapters.title: The Cannery at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Wendell and Cass's POV. Following the recipe card's burned corner—actually a map fragment—to the derelict cannery, they find signs someone's been living there: blankets, canned food, a second recipe card in Priya's handwriting. Emotional beat: hope with a physical address.

chapters.title: Caught on Camera
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The gray van's driver—Marrow Holdings' fixer, Mr. Latch—confronts Wendell in the school parking lot with photos of them breaking into the hall. He offers the same deal as Corliss: walk away, and the family's problems disappear. Wendell stalls, heart hammering, and says yes. Emotional beat: Wendell's careful mask used as a weapon—and the self-loathing that follows.

chapters.title: The Double Agent
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Playing the bought-off kid, Wendell keeps attending committee meetings, copying ledger pages and learning the prom's logistics: the guest book where every attendee's 'pledge' is recorded, the scholarship announcement ritual. Corliss begins trusting them with real documents. Emotional beat: the invisible kid becoming the most dangerous person in the room.

chapters.title: Birdie's Cake
chapters.summary: Birdie's POV. Birdie, drafted to help bake the marzipan cake, hides in the hall kitchen and witnesses Corliss and Latch burning a box of old ledgers. Birdie photographs it on a cracked phone and tells no one but Wendell. Emotional beat: the youngest sibling carrying the heaviest secret; evidence secured by accident.

chapters.title: Devi Runs
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi, done waiting, goes to the cannery alone and is followed by Latch. Cass intervenes, and in the scramble Devi finds Priya's hiding place—a cannery loft—but she refuses to come out. Emotional beat: Devi's fury that Priya chose hiding over home; Priya's shame at what she was made to sign.

chapters.title: What They Made Priya Sign
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya emerges and tells the truth: she found Marrow Holdings' ownership—Corliss's family and three trustees—and they cornered her, made her sign a gag agreement and a fake 'ran away' statement, and kept her phone. She stayed hidden because she believed they'd hurt Devi. Emotional beat: the missing friend found, broken by the machinery of 'tradition.'

chapters.title: A Gag Order and a Gun Rack
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The gag agreement is airtight; going to the sheriff is useless—Sheriff Daneau is a fund trustee. But Priya kept a copy of the original ledgers hidden in the community hall's time capsule, scheduled to be opened at prom. Emotional beat: the trap and the key are the same object; everything now hinges on prom night.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Revolution
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. The group plans: get the time capsule opened publicly, get the ledgers to the alumni and the newspaper, keep the family safe from Latch. Cass volunteers to be the decoy because they have 'nothing left to lose,' and Wendell refuses to let anyone be disposable. Emotional beat: found family forged in the planning; no one gets spent.

chapters.title: The Dress Code
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell, who never planned to attend, gets fitted for prom attire with Mom's help—her one gift to them. Fitting scene becomes a quiet reckoning: Wendell has spent twelve years dressing to be unseen. Emotional beat: choosing visibility as an act of love.

chapters.title: Latch Tightens
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Latch escalates: Theo's scholarship application is 'lost,' Mom's hospital schedule is suddenly cut, and a code-violation notice appears on the Amberdale house. The message is clear—cooperate or be dismantled. Emotional beat: the price of survival itemized; Wendell nearly breaks.

chapters.title: The Alumni Stand Up
chapters.summary: Wendell and Priya's POV. Priya's gag agreement has a loophole—she can't speak, but the alumni can. Wendell spends two days visiting every 'winner,' and eleven agree to tell their stories on prom night if the ledgers surface publicly. Emotional beat: the town's discarded kids becoming an army.

chapters.title: Prom Eve
chapters.summary: Birdie's POV. The night before: the hall glows, the cake is finished, and the family eats dinner together like nothing is coming. Birdie, who still loves the prom, asks Wendell if the tradition can be saved or only destroyed. Wendell answers: rebuilt, with the truth as its foundation. Emotional beat: tenderness before the storm; stakes made human.

chapters.title: The Guest Book
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Prom night begins. Wendell, wearing committee credentials, signs the guest book and watches Corliss work the crowd, every handshake a transaction. The time capsule ceremony is scheduled for ten o'clock. Wendell's hands shake as the plan's point of no return approaches. Emotional beat: terror dressed in formalwear.

chapters.title: The Announcement
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. During the scholarship presentation, Corliss names a winner—Theo's name, a bribe in front of the whole town. Wendell walks onto the stage, takes the microphone, and instead of accepting, tells the town that the scholarship fund has been stealing from them for fifty years. Emotional beat: the careful kid's voice, finally loud; the room's stunned silence.

chapters.title: Capsule and Consequence
chapters.summary: Priya and Cass's POV. As Corliss tries to cut the power and Latch moves toward Wendell, Cass and Priya force the time capsule open onstage—the ledgers, the alumni's statements, and Birdie's photos of the burning box spill into public view. The alumni stand up one by one. Emotional beat: chaos becoming testimony; the tradition's machinery exposed in its own temple.

chapters.title: Latch and the Fire Exit
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Latch corners Wendell backstage with the burned recipe card's twin—the last document linking Corliss to the siphon. Wendell stalls him while Devi livestreams the confrontation from the catwalk. When the crowd surges backstage, Latch flees; the sheriff, exposed, can't protect him. Emotional beat: Wendell's invisibility weaponized one last time—then discarded.

chapters.title: Corliss Unmasked
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. Cornered by the alumni, the newspaper, and her own family's history, Corliss justifies the fund as 'keeping the town alive'—the mill owners' descendants genuinely believing they own the future. She resigns on the hall's stage as the marzipan cake is cut and shared. Emotional beat: the villain as true believer; tradition as a story people tell to avoid guilt.

chapters.title: After the Last Dance
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Dawn after prom: the state attorney's office calls, Marrow Holdings is under investigation, and the scholarship will be rebuilt with community oversight—with Wendell's name on the charter. Priya and Devi go home. Wendell sleeps for fourteen hours. Emotional beat: the exhale; survival finally meaning more than endurance.

chapters.title: The Recipe, Restored
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass, Priya, and Wendell restore the marzipan recipe to its union origins, adding the names of every kid the fund erased—including Cass's—baked into the cake's presentation for next year. The cannery loft becomes a youth center's first room. Emotional beat: grief converted into inheritance; the tradition saved by changing what it's for.

chapters.title: What Wendell Kept
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell returns the committee stipend, declines the 'clean' version of the scholarship, and instead takes a part-time job and the town's offer of childcare support for the family. Mom picks up a day shift; Theo and Birdie get a childhood. Emotional beat: Wendell learning that accepting help isn't losing; the careful kid learning to be cared for.

chapters.title: Keys for Everyone
chapters.summary: Birdie's POV. One year later: Birdie narrates the new Founder's Day prom—messier, louder, open to everyone, with Priya as its youngest-ever organizer. Priya gives Wendell a new keyring: keys to the hall, the youth center, and the Amberdale house, 'so nobody has to leave them on a porch again.' Emotional beat: the story's central symbol transformed; found family holding every key.

chapters.title: Prom and Recipe
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Final chapter: Wendell, now a senior, dances at the prom they rebuilt, watches Mom laugh with the alumni, and finally reads the completed recipe card Priya left on the porch a year ago—its last line, hidden under the burn, says: 'For Wendell, who was always taking care of everyone. Time someone took care of the tradition instead.' Wendell lets go of being careful. Emotional beat: full-circle closure; visibility chosen, family kept, truth made tradition.
